result.topic_en: Riemann derives from a variational (general) equation the condition div η' = −4πρ and the equation ∂λ/∂y = ∂⁴y/∂t⁴, relating gravitational forces to the motion of a space-filling medium in the empty and mass-filled parts of space.
result.transcription:
Also sind sämmtl. Bedingungen zur
Hervorbringung der Lichterscheinungen
erfüllt (da nur die Gesetze derselben nur
für den leeren Raum bekannt sind).
Diese letzte Gleichung [-enthält-] {+zeigt+} ferner die
Ursache der Gravitationskräfte in der
Bewegung des geschlossenen [?] Raumes [-an-] für
den von ponderabler Masse leeren Theil des
geometrischen Raumes.
Die allgemeine Gleichung enthält ferner
die Bedingung:
$-\delta\lambda.\left(\frac{\partial\eta_1'}{\partial\eta_1}+\frac{\partial\eta_2'}{\partial\eta_2}+\frac{\partial\eta_3'}{\partial\eta_3}\right)d\eta_1\,d\eta_2\,d\eta_3\,dt-\delta\lambda.\,dm\,dt=0$
welche dieselbe ist, wie:
$\frac{\partial\eta_1'}{\partial\eta_1}+\frac{\partial\eta_2'}{\partial\eta_2}+\frac{\partial\eta_3'}{\partial\eta_3}=-4\pi\varrho$
außerdem [-folgt-] liegt noch darin, daß
$-\int\left(\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_1}\delta y_1+\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_2}\delta y_2+\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_3}\delta y_3\right)dm\,dt+\int\left(\frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial t^2}.\delta\frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial t^2}+\frac{\partial^2 y_2}{\partial t^2}.\delta\frac{\partial^2 y_2}{\partial t^2}+\frac{\partial^2 y_3}{\partial t^2}.\delta\frac{\partial^2 y_3}{\partial t^2}\right)dm\,dt=0$
also:
$-\int\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_1}\delta y_1\,dm\,dt+\int\frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial t^2}\delta\frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial t^2}dm\,dt$ [-=-] $=-\int\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_1}\delta y_1\,dm\,dt+\int\frac{\partial^4 y_1}{\partial t^4}\delta y_1\,dm\,dt=0$
d.h. daß:
$\left(-\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_1}+\frac{\partial^4 y_1}{\partial t^4}\right)\delta y_1=0$ ist.
Diese Gleichung findet an einem Orte,
wo {+sich+} keine ponderable Masse [-befindet-] ist, immer
Statt, weil dort: $\delta y_1=0$
An einem ponderable Masse enthaltenden
Ort wird sie zur Bedingungsgleichung:
$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_1}=\frac{\partial^4 y_1}{\partial t^4}$
Nun ist $\frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial t^2}$ die Componente der Accelaration
also: $\frac{\partial^2 y_1}{\partial t^2}=\frac{\partial U}{\partial y_1}=\eta_1'$.
$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_1}=\frac{\partial^2\frac{\partial U}{\partial y_1}}{\partial t^2}=\frac{\partial^2\eta_1'}{\partial t^2}$
$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_2}=\frac{\partial^2\frac{\partial U}{\partial y_2}}{\partial t^2}=\frac{\partial^2\eta_2'}{\partial t^2}$
$\frac{\partial\lambda}{\partial y_3}=\frac{\partial^2\frac{\partial U}{\partial y_3}}{\partial t^2}=\frac{\partial^2\eta_3'}{\partial t^2}$
$\lambda=\frac{\partial^2 U}{\partial t^2}$
7

methods.what: Variation with respect to the Lagrange multiplier λ yields a Poisson-type divergence condition
Integration by parts in time of the variation of acceleration-squared term, giving a fourth time derivative
Equation of condition at places with ponderable mass
Acceleration as gradient of potential U, and identification of λ with the second time derivative of U
